title: A square power for a pointed smooth family with geometrically integral generic fibre
statement:
Let $S$ be a nonempty affine Noetherian integral scheme [def-pc-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth, def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme, def-pc-integral-scheme] which is normal: every local ring is an integrally closed domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Let $\eta=\operatorname{Spec}k(S)$ be its generic point [def-sc-generic-point, def-sc-function-field]. Let $H\to S$ be a smooth separated group scheme of finite type with geometrically connected fibres [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-connected-scheme]. Thus $H$ has multiplication, identity and inverse satisfying the group identities; separated means the diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]; and $H\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ is nonempty and connected for every algebraically closed field $\Omega$ over a residue field of $S$ [def-pc-fibre-product, def-weil-residue-field]. Let $p:Y\to S$ be smooth, separated and of finite type, with $Y$ integral, an $S$-section $e:S\to Y$ satisfying $pe=\mathrm{id}_S$, and an action $a:H\times_SY\to Y$ satisfying the unit and associativity identities. Suppose the generic fibre $Y_\eta$ is geometrically integral: it remains nonempty, reduced and irreducible after every extension of $k(S)$ [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. Let $L$ be any invertible $\mathcal O_Y$-module [def-sc-invertible-module]. There exists an integer $r\geq1$ such that $M=L^{\otimes r}$ has the following property. For every $S$-scheme $B$, write $Y_B=Y\times_SB$, $q_B:Y_B\to B$, and $M_B$ for the module pullback [def-pc-module-pullback]. For every $g,h\in H(B)=\operatorname{Hom}_S(B,H)$, put $\tau_g(y,b)=(g(b)y,b)$. There is an invertible $\mathcal O_B$-module $N$ and an isomorphism
$$\tau_{gh}^*M_B\otimes M_B\cong\tau_g^*M_B\otimes\tau_h^*M_B\otimes q_B^*N.$$
All tensor products and tensor powers are sheaf tensor products [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. The exponent $r$ is chosen before $B,g,h$. No equivariance of the section $e$, integrality of special fibres of $Y$, properness, or commutativity is assumed.

source.place: Proposition 5.9, final assertion, case (1), and Lemma 5.7; smooth Noetherian affine-base specialization; printed pp.14-15 of March 31, 2026 version, read online. Local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: Both $Y\to S$ and $H\to S$ are of finite presentation. Indeed smoothness gives local finite presentation by [lem-pc-smooth-flat], finite type gives quasi-compactness [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and the closed diagonal is quasi-compact: by the affine description in [def-weil-closed-immersion], its inverse image of an affine is affine, hence quasi-compact by the basic-open/unit-ideal argument. This is precisely finite presentation as defined in [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. The identity section of $H$ and [lem-sbc-smooth-section-component-geometrically-irreducible] give an open $U\subseteq H$ with geometrically irreducible fibres containing every point of the fibre component through the identity. The fibres are connected by hypothesis, so this component is the entire fibre and $U=H$. The fibres are also geometrically reduced by [sbc-lem-smooth-geometrically-reduced]. Thus all fibres of $H$ are nonempty geometrically integral, using the definitions [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible, def-pc-integral-scheme]. No analogous assertion is made about special fibres of $Y$.

source.place: Proposition 5.9(1), geometric hypotheses; smooth specialization; cf. the existing normal-group-square-power proof, Step 1.

proof.text: Put $C=Y\times_SH\times_SH$, ordered as $(y,u,v)$, $P=Y\times_SY\times_SH\times_SH$, ordered as $(y_0,y_1,u_0,u_1)$, and $Z=P\times_SH$, with projection $\pi:Z\to P$. Build each product by adjoining one factor at a time. Every new projection is smooth by [lem-pc-proper-base-change](2); iterating [lem-trf-smooth-composition] makes each product smooth over $S$. Hence $P$ is flat and locally of finite presentation over $S$ by [lem-pc-smooth-flat]. Starting from normal $S$, [lem-sfb-smooth-normal-ascent] along the projections gives normal products. Starting from locally Noetherian $S$, [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft] along the same projections gives locally Noetherian products, since local finite presentation implies local finite type directly from finite generators. After base change to $k(S)$ the factors remain smooth, separated and of finite presentation by [lem-pc-proper-base-change](2), [lem-weil-pbc-separated-base-change], and [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](3). The factors $Y_\eta,H_\eta,H_\eta$ are geometrically integral by hypothesis and Step 1. Repeated [lem-sc-geometrically-irreducible-product] makes $P_\eta$ geometrically irreducible; its smoothness and [sbc-lem-smooth-geometrically-reduced] make it geometrically reduced. In particular $P_\eta$ is nonempty and integral.

source.place: Tag 034F, lemma-normal-local-smooth; the cited product, smoothness and Noetherian permanence statements. This verifies the parameter-base hypotheses used in Guo Proposition 5.2(i).

proof.text: The scheme $P$ is integral even though special fibres of $Y$ may be disconnected. Here is the elementary localization argument of Stacks Tag 0BCM (lemma-flat-over-integral-integral-fibre). For a nonempty affine $W=\operatorname{Spec}D\subseteq P$ mapping into $V=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq S$, $R$ is a domain and $D$ is flat over $R$ by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-affine-criterion]. By [lem-trf-flat-module-torsionfree-domain], localization gives an injection $D\hookrightarrow D\otimes_R\operatorname{Frac}(R)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] the latter is the ring of the open $W_\eta$ of $P_\eta$. It is nonzero by the injection, and a domain because $P_\eta$ is integral. Thus $D$ is a domain. Such $W$ form a basis, and every nonempty open of $P$ meets $P_\eta$. Any two nonempty opens therefore meet in the irreducible $P_\eta$. Consequently $P$ is nonempty, reduced and irreducible, which is integrality [def-pc-integral-scheme]. Moreover $P\to S$ is surjective: $y_0=y_1=e(s)$ and $u_0=u_1=1_s$ give a section. The generic point $\xi$ of $P$ therefore maps to $\eta$: its image specializes to every point of $S$, by continuity and surjectivity, and $S$ has a unique generic point.

source.place: Tag 0BCM, lemma-flat-over-integral-integral-fibre; the displayed affine-local argument and elementary generic-point reasoning.

proof.text: Let $b:C\to Y$ be $b(y,u,v)=uv^{-1}y$, and set $A=b^*L$. It is invertible: pull back local rank-one generators [def-sc-invertible-module, def-pc-module-pullback]. For an invertible $F$ on $C$, abbreviate its pullbacks to $Z$ as $F_{ab}=F(y_a,u_b,v)$ and set $E(F)=F_{00}\otimes F_{11}\otimes F_{01}^{-1}\otimes F_{10}^{-1}$. Apply [lem-sfb-field-product-square-power] over $k(S)$ with factors $X_1=Y_\eta$ and $X_2=X_3=H_\eta$ and line $A_\eta$. All three factors have the required smooth separated finite presentation and geometric integrality by Steps 1-2. It gives one integer $r\geq1$ and an invertible $Q_\eta$ on $P_\eta$ with $E(A^{\otimes r})_\eta\cong\pi_\eta^*Q_\eta$. The identification follows by expanding the four factors: pullback commutes with tensor products, tensor powers and duals, as is checked on local rank-one generators. Set $M=L^{\otimes r}$ and $F=b^*M=A^{\otimes r}$. This choice of $r$ precedes all test schemes and group-valued points.

source.place: Proposition 5.2(ii), generic-field power, applied in the order X,Y,Z = Y,H,H as in Proposition 5.9(1).

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-normal-noetherian-generic-line-pullback] to $\pi:Z\to P$ and the invertible line $E(F)$. The base $P$ is normal integral locally Noetherian by Steps 2-3, and $Z$ is locally Noetherian by Step 2. The map $\pi$ is smooth, hence flat and locally of finite presentation and therefore locally of finite type. For any $p\in P$ over $s\in S$, $Z_p=H_s\times_{\kappa(s)}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(p)$ is integral and nonempty by Step 1. Finally, $\xi\to P$ factors through $P_\eta$ by Step 3. Pulling the Step 4 isomorphism to $Z_\xi$ gives $E(F)|_{Z_\xi}\cong\pi_\xi^*(Q_\eta|_\xi)$. An invertible module over the field $k(P)$ is a one-dimensional vector space and has a basis [def-sc-invertible-module]; hence this last pullback is trivial. These are all the hypotheses of the cited generic-line statement, which yields an invertible $Q$ on $P$ and $E(F)\cong\pi^*Q$. Crucially the integral fibres used here are those of $H$, not those of $Y$.

source.place: Tag 0BD7, lemma-in-image-pullback, hypotheses (1)-(5) and conclusion; Guo Proposition 5.2(i) in the reordered factors.

proof.text:
On $Y^2\times_SH^2\times_SH^2$, define $\mathcal C$ to be the pullback of $E(F)$ at $v=v_0$ tensored with the inverse of its pullback at $v=v_1$. Step 5 makes $\mathcal C$ trivial, since the two maps to $P$ are identical and the factors $Q$ and $Q^{-1}$ cancel. For $T=H^4$ with coordinates $(u_0,u_1,v_0,v_1)$, define on $Y\times_ST$ the line
$$D(y)=F(y,u_0,v_0)\otimes F(y,u_1,v_1)\otimes F(y,u_0,v_1)^{-1}\otimes F(y,u_1,v_0)^{-1}.$$
Expanding both expressions gives $\mathcal C\cong D(y_0)\otimes D(y_1)^{-1}$: the positive factors are $F(y_0,u_0,v_0),F(y_1,u_1,v_0),F(y_0,u_1,v_1),F(y_1,u_0,v_1)$, and the four complementary factors have negative sign. Reordering tensor factors is allowed for modules; no group factors are reordered. All pullback, dual and cancellation identities follow on rank-one local frames [def-pc-module-pullback, def-sc-invertible-module, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product].

source.place: Section 5.1: square implies cube and symmetry of the eight-factor cubical difference; Proposition 5.9(1), change of factor order.

proof.text: Let $q:Y\times_ST\to T$ be projection and let $e_T:T\to Y\times_ST$ be the pullback of the given section $e$. Set $K=e_T^*D$, an invertible module on $T$ [def-sc-invertible-module, def-pc-module-pullback]. Pull the trivialization $D(y_0)\otimes D(y_1)^{-1}\cong\mathcal O$ of Step 6 back along $(y,t)\mapsto(y,e(s),t),\quad s\text{ the common image in }S$. Pullback composition identifies it with $D\otimes q^*K^{-1}\cong\mathcal O$. Tensoring by $q^*K$ and canceling gives $D\cong q^*K$. This uses only that $e$ is an $S$-section. Its image is not required to be fixed by the action.

source.place: Section 5.1: cube implies square when the third factor has a section; Proposition 5.9(1), return to the order H,H,Y.

proof.text:
Fix any $S$-scheme $B$ and $g,h\in H(B)$. Define $t:B\to T=H^4$ by $t=(g,1,h^{-1},1)$. Pull the isomorphism $D\cong q^*K$ back along $Y_B\to Y\times_ST$ induced by $t$. The four composites with $b$ in the definition of $D$ are $ghy,y,gy,hy$, respectively. The unit, inverse and associativity identities of the action give these equalities without commuting $g$ and $h$. Thus the pullback is
$$\tau_{gh}^*M_B\otimes M_B\otimes(\tau_g^*M_B)^{-1}\otimes(\tau_h^*M_B)^{-1}\cong q_B^*t^*K.$$
Set $N=t^*K$ and tensor by $\tau_g^*M_B\otimes\tau_h^*M_B$. Evaluation of a line against its dual cancels the inverse factors and gives exactly the asserted isomorphism [def-sc-invertible-module, def-pc-module-pullback]. The same $r$ from Step 4 works for every $B,g,h$, including nonreduced or non-Noetherian $B$, since this is pullback of one global isomorphism.

source.place: Lemma 5.7, explicit square-difference specialization; Proposition 5.9(1), final assertion.

lean.statement: theorem exists_pointedGenericIntegralAction_square_tensorPower (S : Scheme.{u}) [IsAffine S] [IsLocallyNoetherian S] [IsIntegral S] (hS : ∀ s : S, IsDomain (S.presheaf.stalk s) ∧ IsIntegrallyClosed (S.presheaf.stalk s)) (H : Over S) [GrpObj H] [Smooth H.hom] [IsSeparated H.hom] [LocallyOfFiniteType H.hom] [QuasiCompact H.hom] [GeometricallyConnected H.hom] (Y : Over S) [Smooth Y.hom] [IsSeparated Y.hom] [LocallyOfFiniteType Y.hom] [QuasiCompact Y.hom] [IsIntegral Y.left] (e : S ⟶ Y.left) (he : e ≫ Y.hom = 𝟙 S) [ModObj H Y] (hη : GeometricallyIntegral (pullback.snd Y.hom (S.fromSpecStalk (genericPoint S)))) (L : Y.left.Modules) [L.IsInvertible] : ∃ r : ℕ, 1 ≤ r ∧ ∀ (B : Over S) (g h : B ⟶ H), ∃ N : B.left.Modules, N.IsInvertible ∧ Nonempty (((tensorPullback (((snd Y B ≫ (g * h)) • fst Y B).left)).obj (L.tensorPow r) ⊗ (tensorPullback (fst Y B).left).obj (L.tensorPow r)) ≅ (((tensorPullback (((snd Y B ≫ g) • fst Y B).left)).obj (L.tensorPow r) ⊗ (tensorPullback (((snd Y B ≫ h) • fst Y B).left)).obj (L.tensorPow r)) ⊗ (tensorPullback (snd Y B).left).obj N))
